profile.address: 2400 Stateline Road West, Southaven, DeSoto County, MS 38671
profile.reading:
This building is not in Memphis. Its mapped footprint sits just south of the Tennessee and Mississippi state line, and the DeSoto County, Mississippi parcel layer returns it unambiguously as parcel 108515000 0000700, 48.60 acres, address 2400 Stateline Road West, in the Stateline Road Industrial Park, zoned M-1, owned by MZX TECH LLC with an owner mailing address of 1450 Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, California, recorded at deed book 1025 page 24710. Tulane Road addresses in Memphis have circulated for this building. Those belong to xAI's separate Colossus 2 site roughly a kilometer north and on the Tennessee side of the line. The municipality here is Southaven, in DeSoto County, Mississippi.

The State of Mississippi named the facility itself. In a January 8, 2026 announcement the governor's office said xAI would invest more than 20 billion dollars in Southaven, called it the largest economic development project in state history, and said the data center would be known as MACROHARDRR, that xAI had purchased and was retrofitting an existing building to house it, that the project would create hundreds of permanent jobs in DeSoto County, that operations were expected to begin in February 2026, and that on completion the company's computing power would approach 2 gigawatts. The Mississippi Development Authority approved xAI for its Data Center Incentive, a sales and use tax exemption on computing equipment and software, and the City of Southaven and DeSoto County are supporting the project through fee in lieu agreements. Property records show the affiliate MZX Tech LLC, formed May 16, 2025, bought this building on December 23, 2025. MZX Tech now holds four DeSoto County parcels totalling roughly 269 acres, all zoned M-1, including the 114.49 acre power plant tract at 2875 Stanton Road.

That power plant is the reason this address is contested. It is on site generation for the campus, not IT load and not a capacity figure, and the two must not be conflated. A notice of intent to sue filed February 13, 2026 for the NAACP counted 27 turbines rated at least 495 megawatts combined, listing 14 SMT-130 units, one M35, and twelve TM2500 units across three generations, and estimated potential annual emissions of 2,508 tons of nitrogen oxides, 236 tons of fine particulates, 837 tons of carbon monoxide and 25 tons of formaldehyde. It alleged the units were built and run from August 1, 2025 without preconstruction, operating, prevention of significant deterioration or hazardous air pollutant permits. The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality had treated them as exempt temporary mobile equipment usable under twelve months. Those are an objector's allegations and a regulator's interpretation, not findings.

What regulators actually did: on March 10, 2026 the Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board voted unanimously to grant a permit for 41 turbines with emission control technology, dispersion modeling and monitoring conditions attached, after a February 17, 2026 hearing at which residents raised noise and air quality objections. The Southern Environmental Law Center appealed that decision on April 9, 2026. The NAACP filed a Clean Air Act suit against xAI and MZX Tech on April 14, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi, case 3:26-cv-00074-MPM-JMV, and moved for a preliminary injunction on May 6, 2026, later amending to cite 57 operating turbines. On June 18, 2026 the Department of Justice moved to intervene on national security grounds. Under a July 30, 2026 agreement with the state, temporary turbines were to begin coming out in August 2026 and be gone by July 2027, with the 41 permitted units installed in their place. A preliminary injunction hearing set for August 24, 2026 was postponed. The matter is open.

profile.community_note: Southaven residents have objected mainly on noise and air quality. Neighbors reported turbine noise from November 2025, and a February 17, 2026 Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality hearing drew a large turnout at which no speaker supported the application. Residents have said their only reliable channel to the company runs through the mayor's office. xAI says it is spending millions of dollars on sound walls, silencers and next generation turbines, that its permitted units carry selective catalytic reduction, and that local air quality continues to meet or exceed federal standards. On the economic side the state describes more than 20 billion dollars of investment and hundreds of permanent jobs in DeSoto County, supported by a Mississippi Development Authority sales and use tax exemption and fee in lieu agreements with the city and county. On September 2, 2026 the Southaven Board of Aldermen approved a further 660,000 square foot xAI building at 8325 Tulane Road with conditions on streetscape, screening trees and perimeter fencing, alongside a 40 million dollar company contribution toward a police and fire training center.
profile.incentives_note: The Mississippi Development Authority certified xAI for its Data Center Incentive, which exempts computing and software equipment from sales and use tax. The City of Southaven and DeSoto County are supporting the project through fee in lieu of tax agreements. The governor's office put the total investment at more than 20 billion dollars and called it the largest economic development project in Mississippi history. Neither the term of the fee in lieu agreements nor the dollar value of the tax exemption is stated in the records reviewed for this page.
profile.regulatory_note: The permitting question is whether the turbines are stationary sources needing Clean Air Act permits or temporary mobile equipment that is exempt. The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality took the exempt view for units run under twelve months, conditionally agreeing on July 29, 2025 and approving an exemption covering 18 turbines in August 2025. xAI applied on January 14, 2026 for a permit covering 41 turbines, and the Mississippi Environmental Quality Permit Board granted it unanimously on March 10, 2026 with control technology, modeling and monitoring conditions. That grant is under appeal by the Southern Environmental Law Center as of April 9, 2026. Separately, the NAACP suit filed April 14, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi asks the court to hold that the interim turbines required preconstruction, prevention of significant deterioration and hazardous air pollutant permits. The Department of Justice moved to intervene for xAI on June 18, 2026, citing national security and testimony from the Defense Department's chief digital officer. No court ruling on the merits or on the preliminary injunction had issued when this page was written.

profile.reading:
This is the original building of xAI's Colossus supercomputer campus in South Memphis, at 3231 Riverport Road, known in permitting and advocacy records as Colossus 1 to distinguish it from a second xAI facility, Colossus 2, built afterward on the Mississippi side of the state line in Southaven and DeSoto County. The site is a former Electrolux appliance factory of about 785,000 square feet, purchased by Phoenix Investors in December 2023 for 35 million dollars. Its existing building shell and proximity to wastewater treatment infrastructure and the Mississippi River let xAI complete initial construction in roughly 122 days by the operator's own account, well under the multi-year timeline typical of new data center construction, with Dell Technologies and Supermicro widely reported to have supplied server and rack infrastructure and Nvidia the GPU hardware. xAI, incorporated by Elon Musk in March 2023, announced the Memphis project publicly on June 5, 2024, describing it as the world's largest supercomputer, brought the facility online later that year, and has used it primarily to train xAI's Grok chatbot alongside workloads tied to X, formerly Twitter, and SpaceX.

The facility's on-site gas turbine power generation has drawn sustained scrutiny from environmental and civil rights groups. In a permit application filed in January 2025, xAI disclosed 15 turbines at the site. Independent aerial imaging obtained by the Southern Environmental Law Center in April 2025 showed 35 turbines actually present, with thermal imagery that month indicating more than 30 operating simultaneously, well beyond what had been disclosed. A 60-day notice of intent to sue delivered in June 2025 reportedly prompted removal of some unpermitted turbines that same month. On July 2, 2025, the Shelby County Health Department issued an air permit authorizing 15 methane gas turbines to operate around the clock, classifying the facility as a new minor source of pollution rather than a major modification and applying a federal Clean Air Act exemption for nonroad engines to the large stationary turbines already installed on site. The Southern Environmental Law Center, the NAACP, and the local group Young Gifted and Green appealed that permit on July 16, 2025 to the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board, arguing the nonroad engine exemption did not legally apply and that the permitting process excluded the surrounding South Memphis and Whitehaven community, a majority Black area in zip code 38109, from any public comment period. Citing NASA satellite data, TIME reported a 3 percent rise in nitrogen dioxide, a smog-forming pollutant, in the area during the period after xAI's turbines came online, with peak pollution episodes observed in late 2024.

No formal public review process preceded the project's initial announcement, and residents in the surrounding neighborhood have described learning about the facility's scale primarily through local news coverage and independent aerial and thermal imaging investigations rather than through any community engagement process from xAI or Shelby County regulators. Because Colossus 2, the associated Mississippi facility with its own separately permitted turbine fleet, sits on a different parcel across the state line, this record's environmental findings are limited to the original Memphis building and its own Shelby County permitting history rather than the combined multi-site campus.
profile.capacity_note: No campus-wide or building-specific MW rating for this facility's gas turbines was found in primary (xAI) or non-aggregator secondary (Southern Environmental Law Center, TIME) sourcing reachable this session. Turbine counts (15 permitted per the July 2, 2025 Shelby County Health Department permit, 35 observed on site per SELC's April 2025 imaging) are documented in the reading without an associated MW figure. A 495 MW figure separately reported for the Mississippi Colossus 2 facility belongs to that distinct site and is not applied here.

profile.address: 5420 Tulane Road, Memphis, Shelby County, TN 38109
profile.reading:
This is xAI's Colossus 2 building in the Scaife area of southwest Memphis, Tennessee, a large single structure on Tulane Road tagged in mapping data at 5420 Tulane Road and identified in federal court filings by the campus address 5400 Tulane Road. It stands just north of the Tennessee and Mississippi state line, and that detail is the single most important fact about the site, because the building's load is in Shelby County while the plant that feeds it is in DeSoto County, Mississippi. xAI announced the second Memphis data center in early March 2025 and began installing computing infrastructure at this site in July 2025. On March 3, 2026 the company filed a construction permit with the Memphis and Shelby County Division of Planning and Development valued at about 659.3 million dollars for a four story, 75 foot building expanding the Colossus 2 site on adjoining ground.

On power the record has to be read carefully, because four different quantities get reported as though they were one. No operator statement or filing reviewed for this page gives an IT load for this building, so none is recorded. Nor is there an established utility service level. In a public update dated May 5, 2025, Memphis Light, Gas and Water said that for the Tulane Road site no final power request had been submitted, that it was not then conducting a system impact study for the site, and that early discussions had ranged anywhere from 260 megawatts to 1.1 gigawatts. That range is a description of conversations, not a service commitment, and it should not be read as capacity. By contrast the utility described the separate Colossus 1 site on Paul R. Lowry Road in firm terms, 8 megawatts from an existing MLGW substation and 142 megawatts from a newly built one, with a further 150 megawatts sought from TVA toward a 300 megawatt target.

What actually powers Colossus 2 sits across the state line. A February 13, 2026 notice of intent to sue filed on behalf of the NAACP identified xAI's plant at 2875 Stanton Road in Southaven, Mississippi, owned by the xAI affiliate MZX Tech LLC, as the source serving Colossus II at 5400 Tulane Road, and counted 27 gas turbines there with a combined rating of at least 495 megawatts as of February 9, 2026. That is on site generation, not compute capacity, and it belongs to the Southaven parcel rather than to this building. xAI's own July 30, 2026 statement describes a 1.2 gigawatt plant under construction with 41 permanent turbines, with temporary mobile units to be removed by July 2027.

The Memphis air permit fight that drew national attention concerned the other campus, not this one. The Shelby County Health Department issued permit 01156-01PC-070225 on July 2, 2025 authorizing 15 turbines at Colossus 1 after receiving more than 1,700 public comments. The NAACP Memphis branch and Young, Gifted and Green, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center, appealed on July 16, 2025, arguing the turbines had been treated as exempt nonroad engines and that the site should have been permitted as an existing major source. The Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board dismissed that appeal on December 15, 2025 on mootness grounds. No comparable Shelby County air permit for turbines at this Tulane Road building appears in the record reviewed here, which is consistent with the generation having been sited in Mississippi.

reading:
xAI is Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, founded in 2023, privately held and not an SEC filer, with offices in Palo Alto, California reported by real estate trade press in January 2026. Following its 2025 merger with X, formerly Twitter, the copyright notice on its own site reads SpaceXAI LLC, reflecting a tighter corporate tie to Musk's other companies. It is in this registry as a hyperscaler, and its three Tennessee rows all sit in Memphis, where the company built the fastest large compute ramp any operator in this dataset has publicly documented.

The flagship is Colossus, built into a former Electrolux manufacturing plant in South Memphis. The build decision was taken in March 2024, announced in June 2024, and the first phase went live in September 2024 with 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs installed in 122 days. By December 2024 the installation had doubled to 200,000 GPUs and peak power draw rose from 150 to 250 megawatts. By June 2025 the configuration was reported as roughly 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200 and 30,000 GB200 accelerators, with a further 110,000 GB200 units planned for a second site, against a stated ambition of reaching a million GPUs. Grid supply came to about 150 megawatts over an existing line, with a second substation adding roughly another 150 megawatts, and xAI requested on the order of 1.1 gigawatts for its expansion.

The reason this operator has an unusually thick public record is what xAI did about the gap between what the grid could deliver and what the buildout needed. It installed gas turbines on the Memphis site and ran them. That is on site generation, and it should not be confused with either critical IT load or the diesel standby plant that most data centres keep. The turbines produce the power, they do not measure the computing. Residents, the Southern Environmental Law Center and local groups argued the turbines had been operating for more than a year without the permits the Clean Air Act requires before construction of a major source. The Shelby County Health Department issued a minor source air permit for fifteen turbines on 2 July 2025, over more than two thousand opposing comments, having treated others as nonroad engines exempt from permitting. The NAACP Memphis branch and Young, Gifted and Green appealed to the Memphis and Shelby County Air Pollution Control Board on 16 July 2025, arguing that up to 35 turbines had run unpermitted and that the site qualified as an existing major source requiring prevention of significant deterioration review. On 16 December 2025 the board dismissed the appeal on mootness grounds rather than on the merits.

The dispute then moved to federal court. In 2026 the NAACP, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice, brought a Clean Air Act citizen suit against xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech over the power plant serving Colossus 2, and filed a motion for a preliminary injunction on 6 May 2026, which was pending as this entry was written. The plaintiffs say that after a notice of violation in February 2026 xAI added six further turbines, bringing that plant to 33 units. That second plant sits in Southaven, Mississippi, outside the Tennessee rows this registry holds for xAI, but it is the same buildout and the same regulatory question.
